en.Play-style preset. It shifts the sliders: Play-style preset. It shifts the sliders below by fixed steps, so with all sliders at their defaults you get the preset, and the sliders still fine-tune around it. Custom = sliders only.
en.Which map edge has an ocean. Auto puts i: Which map edge has an ocean. Auto puts it on a short edge so the land runs along the long side. None gives a landlocked map (then use lakes/rivers for ships and water industries).
en.How far the ocean reaches inland, as a s: How far the ocean reaches inland, as a share of the map length (about 6% to 32%). The coastline wobbles, with bays and headlands.
en.Width of the slope from the shore down t: Width of the slope from the shore down to deep water, for the ocean and lakes. Steep gives deep water close to shore (good for harbours). Gentle gives wide shallows and beaches.
en.Small-scale irregularity of the ocean sh: Small-scale irregularity of the ocean shore (coves, points, small bays), on top of the large bays.
en.Small islands in the ocean, 250 m to 2.5: Small islands in the ocean, 250 m to 2.5 km off the coast.
en.Varies the shoreline steepness along the: Varies the shoreline steepness along the coast and lakes: stretches of wide beaches and shallows alternate with steep drop-offs.
Number of lakes (scales with map area). Lakes are deep enough for ships and host fishing and oil rigs. Very small maps can still get none at low settings.
en.Size of each lake: stamp size 3 km to 10: Size of each lake: stamp size 3 km to 10 km (vanilla 6 km).
en.Number of rivers. Rivers start in the oc: Number of rivers. Rivers start in the ocean or lakes and flow inland, carving valleys through all terrain, including mountains.
en.Width of the large rivers (0.6x to 1.7x): Width of the large rivers (0.6x to 1.7x). Small streams and headwaters keep their natural width; rivers widen downstream, at confluences and at their mouths.
en.Meander strength, from nearly straight t: Meander strength, from nearly straight to looping lowland rivers. Meanders vary in size along the river, scale with river width and are damped in rough terrain.
en.Width of the flat valley floor along riv: Width of the flat valley floor along rivers and of the valley slopes. Wide valleys give easy corridors for rails and roads along rivers.
en.How many side streams branch off the riv: How many side streams branch off the rivers. Streams are narrow and mostly scenic; more of them also means wider main rivers downstream.
en.Adds one large river that crosses the wh: Adds one large river that crosses the whole map from the coast side to the far side (also with Ocean coast None).
en.Chance that a large river reaching the o: Chance that a large river reaching the ocean or a lake splits into a delta of 2 to 4 channels.
en.How much of the land is mountain massif: How much of the land is mountain massif (high plateau with alpine peaks), from none to dominant. Mountains are hard to build on.
en.Height of the alpine peaks above the mou: Height of the alpine peaks above the mountain plateau: about 180 m to 560 m (vanilla about 360 m). Rock and snow textures start at about 330 m and 380 m.
en.Share of the non-mountain land that is f: Share of the non-mountain land that is flat lowland (0 to 14 m relief), where towns, stations, airports and farms fit best. The rest becomes hills and uplands.
en.Height of hills and uplands: about 40 m: Height of hills and uplands: about 40 m to 210 m (vanilla about 120 m). Higher hills make routes harder (more grades, cuts and tunnels).
en.Small-scale undulation of the flat lowla: Small-scale undulation of the flat lowlands: about 1 m to 14 m (vanilla 4 m). Low values are near-perfectly flat for building.
en.Size of the terrain regions (plains, hil: Size of the terrain regions (plains, hill country, mountain areas). Broad gives large continuous regions. Fine gives a patchwork.
en.Tendency for terrain to rise away from t: Tendency for terrain to rise away from the coast side: lowlands near the coast, hills and mountains toward the far side. Off gives a random layout. It also applies when Ocean coast is None.
en.Long, flat-bottomed valleys cut through: Long, flat-bottomed valleys cut through hills and mountains, independent of rivers. They are natural routes for railways and highways.
